coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 13
record.summary: Planned mixed-use block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan; the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 shows two towers up to 280 and 300 ft on this block, the tallest permitted heights on the site, though the D4D's separate height-category text places Block 13 among 'Midrise buildings' (101-145 ft) -- an internal inconsistency in the adopted document that this dossier does not resolve.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land within the former power station site (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram via multi-point real-street georeferencing (see digitization_method), but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area -- see digitization_method). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 via GDAL GCP/TPS georeferencing -- see digitization_method. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third pass) in a single consistent pixel-detection pass across the whole block layout -- see digitization_method. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth pass) after fixing a mis-measured GCP -- see digitization_method.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: The D4D's own Permitted Uses table shows Block 13 permits Residential, Institutional, Retail, Entertainment, AND PDR -- NOT limited to 'infrastructure, utility, and PDR preservation' as sometimes described secondhand. Figure 6.2.3 itself shows a notably tall envelope here: an 85 ft/125 ft base split with 300 ft and 280 ft max upper-height callouts on its two halves -- the tallest permitted heights found anywhere on this site, which is itself worth double-checking against a more current source before treating as final, since it doesn't match this block's 'infrastructure/utility' reputation in casual references at all. No construction-start source found.

facts.value: Residential, Institutional, Retail, Non-Retail Sales/Services and PDR uses permitted (limited PDR uses at the lowest floors); Laboratory and Life Science uses Not Permitted (D4D final Table 3.1.1)
an 85 ft/125 ft base split with two upper-tower callouts of 300 ft max and 280 ft max, per the D4D's Figure 6.2.3 -- see summary for the discrepancy with the D4D's own height-category text
One of three blocks (with 1 and 5) eligible to host the project's single permitted district parking garage (max 90 ft, with a publicly accessible rooftop sports field)
The 2024 annual compliance report's only mention of Block 13 is a preservation design-review requirement for its Illinois Street frontage; no building design review or construction is described
Not listed among the six Phase 1 blocks (2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15) named in the 2024 annual compliance report

images.appeal_note: Color-coded building height plan across the full 15-block site with a clear legend, but the small block-by-block labels don't resolve at card size.

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 13; it is not one of the six buildings named in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list (Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), and no later-phase design review approval was found either.

This dossier's height figures for Block 13 come from this repository's own visual reading of the D4D's Figure 6.2.3 diagram, cross-checked against this repository's existing geometry file (potrero_block_13.geojson), which independently flagged the same 300 ft/280 ft figures as surprising for a block otherwise described in casual references as infrastructure/utility/PDR. The D4D's own Standard 6.2.2 places 'Block 13' in its 'Midrise buildings (101-145 feet)' list, which conflicts with the figure. This is a genuine internal inconsistency in the adopted Design for Development, not a transcription error by this project; flagged for the repository owner rather than resolved here.
